output.brief: FCR fell because of the 14 April Finance change, not the new starters. It cut the in-call credit limit from £100 to £25 and automatically sends larger billing adjustments to the Billing Resolution team. The referral share of billing calls jumped from 7% to 54% in the same week. Referred calls resolve at about 33%, against 82% for non-referred, and both rates are unchanged. Billing share and FCR fell only in the billing category. Referral rates are about equal across tenure bands (56%, 54%, 53%). Tenured agents' FCR fell by the same amount as everyone else's. Tariff enquiries resolve as well as before, and other contact reasons are flat. The IVR and workload explanations are not supported, although I haven't tested them directly. Don't put the April intake on performance plans: the evidence doesn't point at them. Instead, agree a revised credit limit with Finance, with post-call sampling of credits. Trial it on two teams for six weeks and track FCR and unsupported credits, as the financial controller's note allows. Confidence is high on the main cause and moderate on the secondary links, such as complaints. Don't pause the IVR work on this evidence.
